summary: Marine operations professional with twelve years across a ferry deck and a remote lighthouse station. First point of contact for the coastguard on 14 incidents since 2019; plans and runs supply landings, stores and a consumables budget; keeps a first-order light and its generator in service (six years without an unplanned outage). Reports daily, and built the telemetry export the Lights Board schedules its maintenance from.

experience.org: Northern Isles Lights Board, Skerra Head Lighthouse
bullets: Coordinated 14 incidents with the coastguard by VHF since 2019, including three helicopter medical evacuations — the station's first point of contact for emergency services.
Managed the station's stores and supplies: four supply landings a year planned end to end with the supply vessel's master, and a consumables and spares budget of about £40,000 a year.
Kept a first-order rotating light, its fog signal and the standby generator in service as sole keeper: six years without an unplanned outage (2018–2024).
Wrote the 40-page station handbook and trained five relief keepers on it; weather observations reported every three hours to the national meteorological service.

Deck crew on a 40-metre ro-ro ferry, six crossings a day; bosun's mate from 2016 with the deck department's daily checks; radio watch on the bridge with the GMDSS General Operator's Certificate (2014) and STCW basic safety training (2013, renewed 2018).

projects.org: Telemetry for a lighthouse station · personal project
bullets: Raspberry Pi logger in Python with three years of continuous data on fog-signal activations and generator hours; the Lights Board's engineering office plans its maintenance visits from its monthly export.
